title: 과거경험 메인 포인트 3요소 & embarrassed 오용 — 오픽노잼 019
summary: 과거경험 카테고리 메인 포인트 3요소: ① 무슨 일(what) ② 기분(good/bad) ③ 왜 그런 기분(why) — 셋 다 있어야 crystal clear
주제는 첫 문장에서 바로 명확하게 — 마지막에 갑자기 'beach'를 던지면 채점관이 메인 포인트를 못 잡는다
'embarrassed'는 창피한/부끄러운(쪽팔리다)의 뜻 — 한국인이 자주 shocked/flustered 상황에 잘못 사용함
메인 포인트 연습법: 과거경험 질문 10개에 메인 포인트만 답하고, 3요소 다 있는지 확인 — 6번째에 빠지면 처음부터 다시
Habit 카테고리와 달리 과거경험은 3요소 모두 필요 — Habit은 하나로 충분

keyExpressions.en: I was shocked because we hadn't seen each other for two or three years.
keyExpressions.note: 메인 포인트 3요소 완성형: what(saw ex) + feeling(shocked) + why(2-3 years)

keyExpressions.en: I didn't know what to do.
He approached me and said hello, and it was so awkward.

keyExpressions.note: 주의: shocked/flustered를 embarrassed로 쓰는 건 오류 — embarrassed는 쪽팔리다

keyExpressions.en: Be crystal clear about it right from the beginning.
keyExpressions.note: 메인 포인트 원칙 — 주제를 마지막에 던지면 채점관이 놓침

keyExpressions.en: Even though it was cold, we felt warm anyway.
keyExpressions.note: 대조 표현: even though A, B anyway — 감정 묘사에 효과적

cards.back: ① What happened ② How I felt (good/bad) ③ Why I felt that way
cards.example: I saw my ex at the bar → I was shocked → because we hadn't seen each other for years

cards.back: I was shocked because we hadn't seen each other for two or three years.
cards.example: Past experience main point: saw ex-boyfriend + shocked + why

cards.back: I didn't know what to do.
cards.example: I saw my ex sitting with my current boyfriend and I didn't know what to do.

cards.back: He approached me and said hello.
cards.example: He approached me and said hello, and it was so awkward.
Wrong: I was embarrassed when I saw my ex. → Right: I was shocked / I didn't know what to do.

cards.back: Even though it was cold, we felt warm anyway.
cards.example: Central Park was in winter — even though it was cold, we felt warm anyway because we loved each other.

cards.back: Be crystal clear about your main point right from the beginning.
cards.example: Don't throw 'beach' at the end — say it in the first sentence so the grader knows what you're talking about.
